title: Botanical Light Studio: Material Energy Conservation
description: A barn lamp illuminates a translucent plant in a dark studio. The user manipulates the lamp's anisotropic material properties and emission intensity, which physically couples to the plant's diffuse transmission response. An energy budget is conserved: boosting lamp emission drains from a shared energy pool, while adjusting the plant's transmission scattering redistributes absorbed light. Full undo/redo tracks all parameter changes across both objects.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load AnisotropyBarnLamp.glb centered at (-1.5, 0, 0) and DiffuseTransmissionPlant.glb at (1.5, 0, 0). Set a dark background (0x0a0a0f). Camera at (0, 2, 5) looking at origin. Add a dim ambient light (0.05) and a point light parented to the lamp model that reacts to user controls.

Implement a shared ENERGY POOL starting at 100 units displayed as a bar at the top of the screen. Create a right-side HTML panel with these coupled controls:
1. Lamp Emission Intensity slider (0-10): increasing costs energy from the pool proportionally.
2. Lamp Anisotropy Strength slider (0-1): adjusts the anisotropy property on the lamp's MeshPhysicalMaterial.
3. Lamp Anisotropy Rotation slider (0-2π): rotates the anisotropic highlight direction.
4. Plant Transmission slider (0-1): adjusts the transmission property; higher values cost energy.
5. Plant Thickness slider (0.1-5): adjusts thickness on the plant material, redistributing how transmission energy scatters.
6. Plant IOR slider (1.0-2.5): changes index of refraction, coupled so that higher IOR reduces effective transmission cost.
7. Color Temperature slider (2700K-6500K): changes the lamp point light color using blackbody approximation, affecting how the plant's subsurface color appears.

Energy conservation law: total energy spent by emission intensity plus transmission must never exceed 100. If one slider would exceed the budget, clamp it and flash the energy bar red. When reducing a value, energy returns to the pool. Changing IOR modifies the transmission energy cost multiplier (higher IOR = cheaper transmission), creating multi-input coupling.

Implement an undo/redo stack (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z) that records each slider change as a state snapshot of all 7 values plus the energy pool. Display undo/redo buttons in the panel. Show the current energy pool numerically and as a gradient bar. Traverse all loaded meshes to find MeshPhysicalMaterial instances and apply property changes in real time. The interaction requires 10-14 steps to fully explore the coupled parameter space while respecting the energy budget.
